key_insight: AREX turns deep research into a recursive verify-and-refine process, using partial verification to guide targeted follow-up research instead of relying on longer search alone.
engineering_relevance: The paper is relevant for building long-horizon research agents because it introduces an autonomous context-compression tool and training strategy that help maintain progress under growing interaction histories.
method: Inner loop: gather evidence and draft a provisional answer.
Outer loop: audit the answer constraint-wise, isolate unresolved claims, and launch targeted follow-up research.
Learn an autonomous context-update tool to compress history into a compact improvement state without an external model.
evidence_signal: AREX is evaluated on BrowseComp, WideSearch, DeepSearchQA, Humanity's Last Exam (HLE), and other reasoning/tool-use benchmarks, where it outperforms comparable-scale baselines and stays competitive with much larger activated models.
watch_item: Recursive self-improvement may be sensitive to verification quality and context-state compression errors, which could propagate mistakes across long-horizon research trajectories.
paper_title: AREX: Towards a Recursively Self-Improving Agent for Deep Research
